lines.text: In October 1347, twelve Genoese ghost galleys drifted into Sicily carrying dead sailors and an invisible nightmare.
Within weeks, the Black Death swept across Europe, striking with agonizing swellings and high fever.
Physicians roamed desolate cobblestone alleys in hooded robes and aromatic beaked masks, powerless against the plague.
Between thirty and sixty percent of Europe's entire population perished, leaving whole villages completely silent.
Yet from this catastrophic collapse of feudalism arose higher wages, peasant autonomy, and the dawn of the Renaissance.
Humanity's darkest hour reshaped the Western world forever. Subscribe to Beyond History for more.
